column2: David's inquiry about a survivor of Saul's house retains the purpose of mercy for Jonathan's sake, without a new blood-relationship restriction.
Ziba's household origin, summons and servant self-identification remain; ordinary royal your does not become divine Thy.
God's mercy remains the expression David proposes to show, and Jonathan's surviving son is identified by injured feet.
Behold, Machir son of Ammiel and Lo-debar remain in Ziba's location answer.
David sends and brings the man from that same named house and place, retaining repeated identification.
Mephibosheth's explicit Jonathan/Saul genealogy, prostration, name call and Here is your servant remain; Here expresses the presentative.

Propose For I will certainly show you mercy after Do not fear, retaining the explanatory hoti and emphatic cognate construction. Jonathan, restored ancestral land and continual table fellowship remain.
The bowed servant's self-comparison to a dead dog remains his speech, not a narrator's description of disability or worth.
David's grant covers everything of Saul and his whole house to your master's son; the kinship wording is not narrowed to an immediate son despite the preceding genealogy.
Propose And Mephibosheth instead of But Mephibosheth for the coordinating kai. Land work, loaves for the master's son, continual royal-table bread, fifteen sons and twenty servants remain.
column3: The relation of estate provision to table provision remains unstated; no additional household recipient is inserted to reconcile them.

column2: Ziba commits his servant obedience to the human lord king, and the narrator explicitly names David's table and comparison with royal sons.
Mica is a young son, and the whole resident household of Ziba serves Mephibosheth; the scope is not limited to Ziba alone.
Jerusalem residence is linked to continual eating at the king's table; both feet remain specified as lame.
The Ammonite king's death and succession of his son Hanun remain in sequence without an extra named predecessor here.
David names Hanun as Nahash's son and proposes reciprocal mercy, then sends servants to comfort him concerning his father.
Propose But has David not for the second question, preserving the adversative alla. Honouring the father and searching, spying and inspecting the city remain the leaders' competing interpretations.
Shaved beards and cloaks halved at the hips remain; half is not moved onto the beards and buttocks is not substituted for hips.
David's response to the men's great dishonour and Jericho waiting until beard growth remain; the return is future.
The selected subject of being put to shame is David's people. Recruitment retains Beth-rehob's twenty thousand infantry, Maacah's thousand and Istob's twelve thousand.
column3: No became odious to David reading or extra Zobah contingent is supplied in this unit.

column2: David dispatches Joab and the whole force, the mighty men, retaining the appositional description rather than an added second army.
Ammon's gate position and the named Syrian/allied forces alone in the field remain distinct deployments.
Joab faces front and rear opposition, chooses from all Israel's young men and arrays against Syria; some supplies the selected subset implicit in choosing from.
The remaining people pass to brother Abishai's command and face Ammon, preserving the two fronts and their leaders.
You all preserves the plural rescue party in the first condition, contrasted with singular you to Abishai in the second, where Joab's group will rescue him.
Singular courage and collective strengthening remain, for our people and our God's cities; the Lord will do what is good in His eyes is future, not an added conditional wish.
Propose the Syrians fled instead of they fled to clarify the collective enemy subject after Joab and his people advance.
column3: Syrians makes explicit the referent inferred from Syria in the preceding clause and the following verse; it is not a separately expressed noun in the flight clause.

column2: Ammon sees Syria's flight, flees from Abishai and enters the city; Joab returns and the group comes to Jerusalem.
Syria's recognition of defeat precedes gathering together; the collective singular/plural shift remains natural in English.
River Chalamak, Ailam and Shobach heading Hadadezer's gathered force remain the selected names and relationships.
column3: No Euphrates or Helam normalization is substituted; the river-name attachment remains a geographical question.

column2: David gathers all Israel, crosses the Jordan and arrives at Ailam, where Syria arrays and fights against him.
Seven hundred chariots, forty thousand horsemen, striking Shobach and his death there remain.
column3: Destroyed/killed distributes the one removal verb according to vehicle and human objects; no alternative infantry count is imported. His force is contextually Hadadezer's, not David's.

column2: All subordinate kings defect to Israel and serve them after defeat; Syria's fear of helping Ammon again closes the selected unit.
